problem:

- $A={{f}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $B={{g}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$
- $C={{h}^{(n)}(x)=\frac{{\text{d}}^{n}}{\text{d}{x}^{n}}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,:\,n\in {N}_{0}}$

examples.problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A = \left\{f^{(n)}(x) = \dfrac{\textrm d^n}{\textrm d x^n}(e^{5x})  \: : \:  n\in \mathbb{N}_0 \right\}$

- $B = \left\{g^{(n)}(x) = \dfrac{\textrm d^n}{\textrm d x^n}(6e^{-x})  \: : \:  n\in \mathbb{N}_0 \right\}$

- $C =  \left\{h^{(n)}(x) = \dfrac{\textrm d^n}{\textrm d x^n}(2e^{x+3})  \: : \:  n\in \mathbb{N}_0 \right\}$
examples.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{5x} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{5x})=5{e}^{5x} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{e}^{5x})=25{e}^{5x} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(25{e}^{5x})=125{e}^{5x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
A = \{e^{5x}, 5e^{5x}, 25e^{5x}, 125e^{5x}, \ldots\}
$$

Consequently, $A$ is infinite.

- The set $B$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & =6{e}^{-x} \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{e}^{-x})=-6{e}^{-x} \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-6{e}^{-x})=6{e}^{-x} \\ {g}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{e}^{-x})=-6{e}^{-x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $B$ contains only two elements:

$$
B = \{6e^{-x}, -6e^{-x}\}
$$

Consequently, $|B| = 2,$ which is finite.

- The set $C$ is also finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & =2{e}^{x+3} \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x+3})=2{e}^{x+3} \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x+3})=2{e}^{x+3} \\ {h}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x+3})=2{e}^{x+3} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $C$ contains only one element:

$$
C = \{ 2e^{x+3} \}
$$

Consequently, $|C| = 1,$ which is finite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only."

feedback.problem:
Which of the following sets are infinite?

- $A={n\in Z\,:\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2})=0}$
- $B={q\in Q\,:\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{q\pi }{2})=0}$
- $C={x\in R\,:\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x\pi }{2})=0}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

We start by finding the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x\pi }{2})=0$ for $x\in R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x\pi }{2} & =m\pi  \\ x & =2m,\,m\in Z\end{aligned}
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets:

- The set $A$ is infinite.Listing the elements of $B$ for different values of $m,$ we have

$$
A={…,-2,0,2,4,…}.
$$

- The set $B$ is infinite. Since $A$ is infinite, and $A⊆B,$ it follows that $B$ is infinite.

- The set $C$ is infinite. Since $B$ is infinite, and $B⊆C,$ it follows that $C$ is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A,$ $B,$ and $C.$"
